title: Vector matroids and symmetric basis exchange
notes: The independent subfamilies of a finite vector configuration define its matroid. A displayed axiom permits simultaneous exchange in two bases.
statement: Let \(E\) be finite. A nonempty family \(\mathcal B\) of equal-cardinality subsets is a matroid basis family if, for \(B_1,B_2\in\mathcal B\) and \(y\in B_2\setminus B_1\), there exists \(x\in B_1\setminus B_2\) such that both \(B_1-x+y\) and \(B_2-y+x\) belong to \(\mathcal B\). This symmetric exchange formulation is equivalent to the usual basis axiom. For a vector configuration, the bases are its maximal independent subfamilies.
reconstruction: Nonemptiness, equal cardinality, and exclusion of the exchanged element from the other basis are explicit.
fate: This is classical matroid theory; the representation and independence definitions are stated in \citet[Theorem 1.6 and \S 1]{oxleybriefly}, while the basis-based bimatroid reformulation is recalled in \citet[Proposition 2.2]{rohrleulirsch2026bimatroids}. It repeats the subject of occurrence 1985-658.12.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the finite nonempty-family and equal-cardinality conventions make the displayed axiom precise.

title: The Fano configuration and characteristic two
notes: The seven-point diagram is to be realized over \(\mathbb F_2\), but not over \(\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\).
statement: The rank-three Fano matroid \(F_7\), whose lines are the dependent triples in \(\mathbb F_2^3\setminus\{0\}\), is representable over a field \(k\) if and only if \(\operatorname{char}k=2\). In particular its seven indicated incidence relations cannot all arise from a rank-three real or complex vector configuration with that matroid.
fate: \citet[Theorem 4.1]{oxleybriefly} states the exact field criterion. The seven nonzero binary vectors give the recorded realization. This is the same exercise as 1985-658.14.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the problem is settled and is an expository obstruction to representability over the specified fields.

title: Which finite matroids are real or complex representable?
notes: The notebook calls the general question of representability over \(\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\) unsolved, without specifying a type of classification.
statement: For a finite rank-\(r\) matroid on \([n]\) with basis list \(\mathcal B\), representability over \(k=\mathbb R\) or \(\mathbb C\) is equivalent to the existence of \(A\in k^{r\times n}\) satisfying \(\det A_B\ne0\) for \(B\in\mathcal B\), and \(\det A_I=0\) for every other \(r\)-subset \(I\). These are finitely many polynomial conditions, and their solvability is decidable over both fields.
reconstruction: The finite-input decision interpretation is made explicit; it is not claimed to supply an efficient or illuminating combinatorial classification.
fate: \citet[\S 2, pp.~15--42, and \S 3, pp.~43--46]{tarski1951decision} explicitly states quantifier elimination over the reals and its complex extension. The nonvanishing conditions can equivalently be encoded by an auxiliary equation \(u\prod_{B\in\mathcal B}\det A_B=1\). Thus the finite decision problem was settled before 1987. Occurrences 1985-658.13 and 1985-658.16 already connect representability with polynomial systems.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, a finite decision procedure exists; the source specifies no stronger structural classification or complexity target that could responsibly be declared open.

title: Matroids representable over every field
notes: The notes say that representability over every field has been characterized.
statement: For a finite matroid \(M\), the following are equivalent: \(M\) is representable over every field; \(M\) has a totally unimodular real matrix representation; and \(M\) has no minor isomorphic to \(U_{2,4}\), \(F_7\), or \(F_7^*\). Such matroids are called regular.
fate: \citet[Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.5]{oxleybriefly} gives the exact equivalences and attributes them to Tutte 1958. The original Tutte paper was located but could not be opened in this run; the checked modern author exposition is therefore the immediate evidence.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the statement is an established characterization, with no new 1987 question recorded.

title: The bimatroid of nonzero minors
notes: For a matrix with row set \(E\) and column set \(F\), the notes retain all pairs of equally sized subsets indexing a nonzero minor.
statement: For a matrix \(A\in k^{E\times F}\), define \(\mathcal R(A)=\{(I,J):I\subseteq E,\ J\subseteq F,\ |I|=|J|,\ \det A_{I,J}\ne0\}\), including \((\varnothing,\varnothing)\) with determinant one. This records joint row-column dependence at every size, rather than just the row and column matroids.
fate: \citet[Example 2.3]{rohrleulirsch2026bimatroids} gives this exact definition and recalls its origin in \citet{kung1978bimatroids}, published in 1978. The latter original remained inaccessible, so its attribution is indirect; the former result was read.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the construction was established before this seminar and has an exact distinguished-basis matroid encoding.

title: An axiom system for bimatroids
notes: The explicit question asks for axioms on the collection of nonzero square minors.
statement: For finite disjoint \(E,F\), a collection \(\mathcal R\) of pairs \((I,J)\) with \(|I|=|J|\) is an abstract bimatroid exactly when \(\{(E\setminus I)\sqcup J:(I,J)\in\mathcal R\}\) is a matroid basis family on \(E\sqcup F\) containing \(E\). Thus nonemptiness, the pair \((\varnothing,\varnothing)\), and the ordinary basis-exchange axiom after this substitution are a complete axiom system. In the matrix case the extended matroid is represented by \([I_E\mid A]\).
fate: \citet[Proposition 2.2 and Example 2.3]{rohrleulirsch2026bimatroids} proves this equivalence in the exposition of Kung\textquotesingle s 1978 theory. This is a later checked source for an older answer, not a 2026 solution date.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the recorded axiomatization problem is solved by an explicit exchange system; abstract bimatroids need not be realizable matrices.

title: The comparison with the uncertain named bimatroid theory
notes: The page asks how a bimatroid notion in Gelfand--Serganova, UMN, relates to a name transcribed tentatively as \ru{Кунтом}.
statement: An exact comparison would require two specified definitions and a map between their objects. The named passage in Gelfand--Serganova and the second surname are not identified unambiguously by the record. Kung is a plausible bibliographic lead, but this cannot determine the missing first definition.
fate: The full English text of \citet{gelfandserganova1987combinatorial} was opened and searched; it develops ordinary and Coxeter matroids, but no occurrence of bimatroid identified the intended definition. \citet{kung1978bimatroids} is a relevant 1978 lead, with its modern formulation checked in \citet{rohrleulirsch2026bimatroids}. Neither fact proves the requested equivalence.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the comparison is indeterminate from the supplied citation and name; this is not a claim that the two theories differ or that an equivalence is unknown.

title: A determinant exchange identity and basis exchange
notes: Equation (6) has a sign \((-1)^{d-i}\), repeats \(y_1\) in the first bracket, and inserts \(x_i\) into the second; the next sentence uses a nonzero summand to obtain exchange.
statement: For \(x_1,\ldots,x_d,y_1,\ldots,y_d\in k^d\), with brackets denoting ordered determinants, \[[x_1,\ldots,x_d][y_1,\ldots,y_d]=\sum_{i=1}^d[y_i,x_2,\ldots,x_d]\,[y_1,\ldots,y_{i-1},x_1,y_{i+1},\ldots,y_d].\] If both left factors are nonzero, some summand is nonzero, proving simultaneous exchange of \(x_1\) with a suitable \(y_i\).
reconstruction: The insertion positions are fixed exactly, so no additional alternating sign is needed. \oursComputed{} The independent checks are recorded in the early-record verification log.
fate: The corrected identity follows by expanding \(x_1\) in the \(y\)-basis and applying multilinearity; polynomial identity then removes the assumption that the \(y\)-matrix is invertible. It is part of the classical determinant relations recalled in \citet[\S 3, opening paragraph]{speyersturmfels2003tropical}. Direct symbolic checks give a counterexample to the literal notebook expression.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the intended exchange argument is valid after correcting the indices and the redundant sign.

title: All relations among maximal minors
notes: The notes claim that equation (6) supplies all relations among the determinant generators.
statement: Let \(S=k[p_I: I\subseteq[n],\ |I|=r]\), and let \(S\to k[a_{ij}]\) send \(p_I\) to the corresponding maximal minor of a generic \(r\times n\) matrix. Its kernel is the Pl\"ucker ideal, generated by the full family of quadratic Pl\"ucker relations. One erroneous identity or one chosen instance does not by itself generate this ideal.
reconstruction: The generic matrix, coefficient ring, homomorphism, and full relation family are specified.
fate: \citet[\S 3, opening paragraph]{speyersturmfels2003tropical} explicitly states the integral version and quadratic generation as a classical fact. The notebook\textquotesingle s assertion is correct only when (6) denotes the correctly indexed family of determinant exchanges, with the generic maximal-minor interpretation fixed.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the defining relations of the Grassmannian are established; the source formula requires the preceding emendation.

title: Writing the syzygy chain for a fixed Plücker ring
notes: The requested Hilbert syzygy chain passes from determinant generators to relations and then to relations among relations; part (a) asks to write the whole chain.
statement: For specified integers \(0<r<n\) and a field \(k\), the natural algebraic interpretation is a graded free resolution of \(S/I_{r,n}\) over \(S=k[p_I:|I|=r]\). A finite such resolution exists, with length at most \(\binom nr\), by Hilbert\textquotesingle s syzygy theorem. Finite polynomial presentations permit effective syzygy computation. The record does not specify minimality, characteristic, equivariance, or whether a uniform closed formula is required.
reconstruction: A fixed generic Pluecker ring is a limited interpretation of the preceding determinant discussion, not a supplied source hypothesis.
fate: The finite-existence bound follows from \citet[Proposition 10.114.2, Tag 00OQ]{stacks2026foundations}. \citet[Chapter 7, \S 7.3]{weyman2003syzygies} specifically treats syzygies of Pl\"ucker ideals; the chapter description was checked, not a full resolution formula. Consequently neither that metadata nor the general theorem is presented as verification of a particular uniform chain intended by the speaker.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the finite existence and effective fixed-input task are settled; the stronger intended presentation is not specified well enough to assign it an open-problem status.

title: Discretizing the whole syzygy chain
notes: Part (b) asks to discretize the whole chain, with the gloss to write combinatorial relations.
statement: No combinatorial objects, equivalence relation, coefficient theory, or criterion for recovering the algebraic syzygies is given. Thus the requested discretization is not a uniquely defined mathematical construction; the existence of a graded free resolution alone does not supply it.
fate: The Pl\"ucker-syzygy literature located through \citet[\S 7.3]{weyman2003syzygies} addresses algebraic resolutions. Its metadata does not identify the extra combinatorial target in this sentence, and no exact publication match was found.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the omitted meaning of discretization prevents a definite solved or open classification.

title: What information remains beyond the row and column matroids?
notes: The notes suggest constructing a bimatroid from two matroids, then warn that a bimatroid contains additional information and ask what it is.
statement: The pair of row and column matroids does not determine the bimatroid. Over \(\mathbb R\), \(I_2\) and \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) both have free row and column matroids of rank two, but the first has two zero \(1\times1\) minors and the second has none. The extra data are the compatible joint ranks \(\rho(I,J)=\operatorname{rank}A_{I,J}\), equivalently all nonzero square-minor pairs.
reconstruction: The two matrices and the joint-rank answer supply an explicit solution; the source does not contain this example. \oursComputed{} The independent checks are recorded in the early-record verification log.
fate: The counterexample is computed directly. \citet[Proposition 2.6]{rohrleulirsch2026bimatroids} gives the relative-rank characterization and its equivalence with the extended matroid. It also explains why separate row and column restrictions lose joint incidence data. The final cohomological motivation in the notes specifies no separate invariant or theorem.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the insufficiency of two matroids has an elementary witness and a precise joint-rank description.

title: The two presentations of the type-A Hecke algebra
notes: Idempotents \(e_i\) satisfy the modified braid relation; the exercise changes to \(\sigma_i=(q+1)e_i-1\).
statement: For \(q\in\mathbb C^\times\), \(q\ne-1\), put \(\tau=q/(q+1)^2\). The relations \(e_i^2=e_i\), \(e_ie_j=e_je_i\) for \(|i-j|>1\), and \(e_ie_{i+1}e_i-\tau e_i=e_{i+1}e_ie_{i+1}-\tau e_{i+1}\) become \((\sigma_i-q)(\sigma_i+1)=0\), the ordinary braid relation, and distant commutativity. The \(\sigma\)-presentation itself also makes sense at \(q=-1\).
reconstruction: Nonzero q and exclusion of minus one state the domain used by the cited paper; the standard presentation extends further.
fate: \citet[\S 1, equations (1a)--(1c)]{kerov1987realizations} uses these exact generators. The change of generators is invertible only for \(q\ne-1\), a restriction hidden by the notebook\textquotesingle s parameter formula.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the two presentations agree on their stated common domain.

title: Dimension and symmetric-group specialization
notes: At \(q=1\) the algebra is \(\mathbb C[S_N]\); the next exercise asks for \(\dim H_N(q)=N!\).
statement: In the standard presentation, \(T_w=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\) for a reduced expression \(w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}\) is well defined, and \(\{T_w:w\in S_N\}\) is a basis of \(H_N(q)\). Consequently \(\dim H_N(q)=N!\). At \(q=1\), \(T_i^2=1\) and the algebra identifies with \(\mathbb C[S_N]\).
fate: \citet[\S 1, p.~156]{kerov1987realizations} records the dimension and specialization in the already established theory. The same Hecke-basis topic occurs in 1979-483.2.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the dimension is independent of the parameter; semisimplicity is a separate issue.

title: The modular analogy and exceptional parameters
notes: Dipper--James is recommended under the handwritten name Tipper; the theory is called analogous to modular symmetric-group representations, even over \(\mathbb C\), followed by the non-root-of-unity assumption.
statement: For \(q\in\mathbb C^\times\), define \(e(q)\) as the least positive integer \(e\) with \(1+q+\cdots+q^{e-1}=0\), or infinity if none exists. Then \(H_N(q)\) is semisimple if and only if \(e(q)>N\). In the semisimple case its simple modules are indexed by partitions of \(N\); at exceptional roots of unity the modular analogy becomes substantive, and simples arise as nonzero simple quotients of Specht modules.
reconstruction: The quantum characteristic makes the informal modular analogy precise without claiming that all generic cases are modular.
fate: \citet[\S 1, p.~156]{kerov1987realizations} states this distinction and attributes it to \citet{dipperjames1986representations}. The publisher confirms January 1986 and pages 20--52; its full result was not read. Kerov\textquotesingle s full statement was read.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the generic hypothesis removes the nonsemisimple cases from the subsequent construction; complex coefficients alone do not ensure semisimplicity.

title: Young diagrams, tableaux, and axial adjacency
notes: Diagrams are partitions, written with column lengths. A tableau is an increasing chain of diagrams, and its axial distance compares the cells containing \(k\) and \(k+1\).
statement: A standard tableau of shape \(\lambda\vdash N\) is a chain \(\varnothing=\lambda^{(0)}\subset\lambda^{(1)}\subset\cdots\subset\lambda^{(N)}=\lambda\), with one cell added each time. If cell \(k\) has row-column coordinates \((i_k,j_k)\), set \(r_k(t)=(i_{k+1}-j_{k+1})-(i_k-j_k)\), \(1\le k<N\). Say \(s\sim_k t\) when their chains agree except possibly at stage \(k\). For \(N\ge2\), the recorded axial parameter is \(h(\lambda)=1+\max_{t,k}|r_k(t)|\).
fate: \citet[\S 2, p.~157]{kerov1987realizations} gives the same definitions with \(k<N\). The notebook\textquotesingle s upper limit \(k\le N\) refers to a nonexistent cell \(N+1\). Partitions also classify conjugacy classes of \(S_N\) by cycle lengths, but that labeling is distinct from the tableau construction.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the chain and axial-distance definitions are standard once the index range and row-column convention are fixed.

title: The one- and two-tableau adjacency blocks
notes: The two assertions distinguish axial distance \(\pm1\) from larger absolute value.
statement: If \(|r_k(t)|=1\), then the only standard tableau \(s\sim_k t\) is \(t\). If \(|r_k(t)|>1\), there is exactly one other such tableau, obtained by interchanging \(k\) and \(k+1\), and it satisfies \(r_k(s)=-r_k(t)\). Thus each adjacency class has one or two elements.
fate: \citet[\S 2, before Definition 1, p.~157]{kerov1987realizations} states this exact combinatorial fact. It follows directly from the increasing row and column conditions for a standard tableau.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the adjacency blocks are the elementary combinatorics behind the representation matrices.

title: Kerov’s tableau matrices
notes: The matrix entry is the square root of the product of two weights when \(s\sim_k t\), and zero otherwise; the theorem says these matrices represent \(H_N(q)\).
statement: For \(q>0\), \(q\ne1\), and \(\lambda\vdash N\), define \(S^{(k)}_{tt}=W_{r_k(t)}\), \(S^{(k)}_{st}=\sqrt{W_{r_k(s)}W_{r_k(t)}}\) for the distinct adjacent tableau, and zero otherwise, taking the nonnegative square root. With the weights of the next item and \(\tau=q/(q+1)^2\), the assignment \(e_k\mapsto S^{(k)}\) satisfies the Hecke relations and realizes the corresponding Specht module. The limit \(q=1\) recovers Young\textquotesingle s orthogonal form. Generic complex parameters also work with coherent square-root choices.
reconstruction: The positive-real case supplies an unambiguous square-root convention; the broader generic-complex statement requires the convention in the original construction.
fate: \citet[\S 2, Definition 1, Theorem 1 and Remarks 1--2, pp.~157--158]{kerov1987realizations} proves the representation. The notebook expressly introduces this as a report on Kerov\textquotesingle s existing work. Its journal date is 1987; an exact earlier circulation day was not established.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, this is an established construction already being expounded; arbitrary independent complex square-root choices should not be substituted for the coherent convention.

title: The rational weights and their corrected identities
notes: The recurrence starts at \(r\ge0\), despite \(W_0\) being undefined, and equation (19) says \(W_rW_{1-r}=1\). Explicit rational formulas follow.
statement: For \(q\ne0,-1\) with the displayed denominators nonzero, and \(r\ge1\), \[W_r=\frac{q(q^{r-1}-1)}{(q+1)(q^r-1)},\qquad W_{-r}=\frac{q^{r+1}-1}{(q+1)(q^r-1)}.\] Then \(W_{-1}=1\), \(W_1=0\), \(W_r+W_{-r}=1\), and \(W_{-(r+1)}=1-\tau/W_{-r}\) for \(r\ge1\). For \(r\ge2\), \(W_rW_{1-r}=\tau\), not one. At \(q=1\) the limits are \(W_{\pm r}=(r\mp1)/(2r)\).
reconstruction: Initial values, valid integer ranges, and the removable q=1 singularity are stated explicitly. \oursComputed{} The independent checks are recorded in the early-record verification log.
fate: \citet[Appendix, equations (P1)--(P5), pp.~166--167]{kerov1987realizations} supplies the recurrence and product identity. Independent rational-function simplification confirms the factor \(\tau\) and the \(q=1\) limits.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the formulas are consistent after correcting the product constant and excluding the undefined zero index; poles require separate limiting representation theory.

title: A Frobenius formula for Hecke characters
notes: After constructing representations, Gelfand asks to find the characters of the Hecke algebra, then turns to the ordinary symmetric-group formula.
statement: In the ring of symmetric functions in \(X\), for generic semisimple \(H_N(q)\), normalized by \((T_i-q)(T_i+1)=0\), define \[Q_r(X;q)=\frac{1}{q-1}[t^r]\prod_j\frac{1-x_jt}{1-qx_jt},\qquad Q_\mu=\prod_aQ_{\mu_a}.\] If \(w_\mu\) is the product of consecutive disjoint cycles of lengths \(\mu_a\), then \[Q_\mu(X;q)=\sum_{\lambda\vdash N}\chi_q^\lambda(T_{w_\mu})s_\lambda(X).\] This gives generic irreducible character values on the standard cycle representatives; at \(q=1\), \(Q_r\to p_r\).
reconstruction: The generic parameter, generator normalization, and cycle representatives make the broad character request precise. \oursComputed{} The independent checks are recorded in the early-record verification log.
fate: \citet{ram1991frobenius} published a precise Frobenius formula in 1991. The checked full formula is \citet[equation (4.10), p.~266, and Theorem 4.11]{halversonram1999bitraces}, after replacing their Hall--Littlewood \(q_r(X;q^{-1})\) by \(q^rq_r/(q-1)\). That paper explicitly credits several independent discoveries, including Vershik--Kerov; this classification makes no priority claim.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the generic Hecke-character problem has explicit symmetric-function formulas. Nonsemisimple root-of-unity simple characters are a different problem, not solved by this generic identity.

title: The ordinary Frobenius character formula
notes: The opening task asks for symmetric-group characters; the closing alternant expands in power-sum products, with the coefficients equal to character values up to a simple constant.
statement: For \(\lambda\vdash N\), \[s_\lambda=\sum_{\mu\vdash N}\frac{\chi^\lambda(\mu)}{z_\mu}p_\mu,\qquad z_\mu=\prod_{r\ge1}r^{m_r(\mu)}m_r(\mu)!,\qquad p_\mu=\prod_a p_{\mu_a}.\] Thus the omitted constant is the centralizer order \(z_\mu\). The alternant quotient is \(s_\lambda\) after reversing the notebook\textquotesingle s increasing exponent convention to \(\lambda_j+n-j\).
reconstruction: The total-degree condition and the exact centralizer factor replace the abbreviated coefficient description.
fate: \citet[Chapter I, \S 7, especially equation (7.3) and the characteristic map]{macdonald1995symmetric} gives the precise Frobenius normalization. This is the classical result already cited in the notebook, not a 1987 invention.
present_status: As of 11 November 2026, the coefficients determine all irreducible symmetric-group characters, with partitions of total size N and the stated normalization.
